name: The Bell Under Brine
pitch: Auntie Pell will pay a fortune for the glass bell of the drowned cathedral. Nobody who went for it has come back.
intro: Lamp Dock at dusk. The tide is turning, and somewhere under your feet a bell you have never heard is ringing very softly. Auntie Pell taps a map on the table: the drowned cathedral, and a glass bell the size of a boat. 'Bring it up,' she says, 'and you'll never owe anyone again.'
secrets: The bell keeps the drowned choir asleep. Whoever rings it calms the choir and stops the Tidewarden; whoever simply takes it wakes the whole cathedral. Auntie Pell sold the same map to a rival crew, the Saltmarks, who drowned in the nave: their lamp and their notes are there. The tide fills the cathedral in six ticks.

sites.name: Lamp Dock
sites.read: Tarred planks, swinging lamps, gulls arguing. Auntie Pell sits at a barrel with a map and a kettle. Below the dock, the water glows faintly green.
sites.notes: Pell offers 50 crowns each, or a share of the bell. A Standard Talk roll gets her to admit she sold the map before; a Gleam gets her to throw in a second lantern. A Standard Lore roll on the map shows the cathedral's bell chamber is reached through the nave.
clues: Pell's map has a second pin-hole, as if it was copied.

sites.name: The Sunken Causeway
sites.read: A road of glass slabs runs down into the dark, lit by your lanterns. Fish scatter. A cold current pulls at your legs.
sites.notes: The current: each diver makes a Standard Brawn + Swim roll or loses 3 Breath. Two glass eels hunt here, hidden until someone strays or fails the current roll.
clues: A torn rope with a Saltmark knot.

rules.say: The current drags a diver off the causeway, straight into the eels' hunting ground: two glass eels uncoil from the dark.

sites.name: The Drowned Nave
sites.read: Pillars of green glass rise into the dark. Rows of pews float a hand above the floor. Somewhere ahead, very quietly, voices are singing.
sites.notes: The drowned choir sleeps in the pews. Loud work or a failed Sneak wakes it. The Saltmarks' lamp and notes are by the altar: the notes say 'Don't take it. Ring it.' A Deep Lore roll reads the hymn carved on the altar, which says the same.
clues: The Saltmarks' notes: 'Don't take it. Ring it.'

rules.say: The singing stops. In the pews, the drowned choir lifts its heads.
The fighting rings through the glass, and the tide answers.

sites.name: The Bell Chamber
sites.read: A round room of glass with the sea pressing on every wall. In the centre hangs a bell of clear glass, big as a boat, ringing faintly by itself. Before it stands a knight of green glass with a blade of moving water.
sites.notes: The Tidewarden attacks anyone who goes for the bell without ringing it. Ringing it properly takes a Deep Nerve + Lore roll (or Standard if they read the hymn). Ringing it stops the Tidewarden and quiets the choir for good; then the bell can be floated up with lines (Standard Brawn + Swim, two divers).

rules.say: Blade on glass: the whole chamber rings, and the tide answers.
The bell rings true, one clear note through the glass. The Tidewarden lowers its blade of water and stands still, its watch over.

quests.text: Bring the glass bell up to Lamp Dock.
Find out what happened to the Saltmark crew.

clocks.name: The Tide
clocks.ticks: When the divers rest, fight loudly, or fail a roll with a Blackout.
clocks.fills: The cathedral floods: every diver must make an Abyssal Brawn + Swim roll to reach the surface.

rules.say: The cathedral floods: every diver must make an Abyssal Brawn + Swim roll to reach the surface.

ending: If the divers ring the bell, the choir sleeps for good and the bell can be brought up: Pell pays, and the lamp guilds want to meet them. If they take it without ringing it, the cathedral wakes and they must flee with whatever they can carry.

reward.other: 50 crowns each, and the lamp guilds' favour if the bell was rung.
